### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **75** documentable anchor(s).

**41** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 60f8149e1a67ca6e00def8e0648c2997d593ddb5`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **76** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 60f8149e1a67ca6e00def8e0648c2997d593ddb5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0af70ca9d2536c8e3cafb087db65085d0b1fc6d4` — the merge of head `ff6392be94fb30c10b74f0855e6e9c844cb76836` into base `60f8149e1a67ca6e00def8e0648c2997d593ddb5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0af70ca9d2536c8e3cafb087db65085d0b1fc6d4 && git checkout 0af70ca9d2536c8e3cafb087db65085d0b1fc6d4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 60f8149e1a67ca6e00def8e0648c2997d593ddb5 ff6392be94fb30c10b74f0855e6e9c844cb76836 && git checkout -B drift-repro 60f8149e1a67ca6e00def8e0648c2997d593ddb5 && git merge --no-ff ff6392be94fb30c10b74f0855e6e9c844cb76836

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 60f8149e1a67ca6e00def8e0648c2997d593ddb5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 60f8149e1a67ca6e00def8e0648c2997d593ddb5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review of #32027 (#31971 PR-1) at head ff6392be: CHANGES.** The required items are seat 3's three. The epic seat adds one obligation for PR-2.

**What passes**
- **Red line 2 is repaired at its source.** With a catalog bound, the evaluator asks only the catalog (`resolveCatalogReference`). A request with an address takes the exact arm. A stale address falls back to D3 and warns (#31974's reading). A name with no address resolves by D3 with no caller, and with two holders it is refused, named and grants nothing. The `metadataService.list('permission')` first-by-name pick is deleted.
- **The context carries `(package, name)`.** `ExecutionContext.permissionSetAddresses` (#31970) is filled by the shared assembler and by all five hand copies. `permissions` keeps its names. `take()` dedupes by holder.
- **The ledger works per holder.** Switching off A's `sales_rep` leaves B's in force. A null-`package_id` row still switches off every holder of the name. That fails closed, so it is never a loosening.
- **Explain and execution report the same holder.** Accepted `everyone` sets resolve from the suggestion row's package (R3).

**Required before PASS (seat 3's asks, which the epic seat shares)**
1. **CONTROL byte-identical.** Restore the admin's `permissionSets` order. Red line 3, reading (b), is "every answer as today". A reordered list is a different answer, even if today's merges ignore order. The request carries the grant order, so keep the old order. Do not just declare the deviation.
2. **Additive exports.** Keep the two changed export signatures callable as before, add the new parameters beside them, and drop the BREAKING.
3. **An end-to-end `everyone`-binding pin.**

**Owed by PR-2 (`Fixes #31971`), before #31698 narrows:** the catalog-less arm (`resolveWithoutCatalog`) still picks first by name. Today that is safe: phase 1 keeps one holder, and the pin shows a booted composition always binds the catalog. Once two holders are possible, though, a catalog-less assembly must not guess. Make it grant nothing for a name two listed sets hold, and warn naming them, with a pin. Alternatively, show that every non-test assembly binds a catalog and make the arm test-only. PR-2 also carries the identities and every grant gate, the delegated-admin gate included, comparing `(package, name)`.
